(b) The token-level A that exists in code, and what it would need:
token-likelihood (cascade_model_manifest.clj:191-216; Lean TokenObservation.lean:31-34 AdjudicationRates, :39 tokenLikelihood): A(o|s) = prod over tokens v of
(v in s ? (v in o ? 1 - falseNeg v : falseNeg v) : (v in o ? falsePos v : 1 - falsePos v)) — it needs {token {:false-neg r :false-pos r}} for EVERY token, exact rationals in [0,1].
Where such rates come from today: efe.clj:1103-1105 — with no :adjudication-rates declared, every token gets {:false-neg 0 :false-pos 0}; observation_rates.clj:122-152 gives

The identity kernel says the observation IS the state. It has no error rate to estimate, and (c) shows there is no pair on any record to estimate one from.
